tip: 'Tidak ada duanya' = there is no second one, i.e. one of a kind: 'sambal ibu tidak ada duanya'.
'Nasi sudah menjadi bubur' = the rice is already porridge: what's done cannot be undone.
'Beliau' = respectful he/she for elders: 'memberi tahu beliau' = tell her (politely).
'Pun' after a noun stresses not even one: 'satu kata pun' = not even a single word.
'Si' before a name marks warmth among friends: 'si Budi' ≈ 'good old Budi'. Casual only – never for elders.
'Si' + adjective names someone by a trait: 'si kecil' = the little one, 'si sulung' = the eldest.
Pets often get 'si' + trait as a name: 'si belang' = the stripey one, 'si putih' = the white one.
'Lagi-lagi' = 'yet again' (mild exasperation): 'lagi-lagi hujan' = it's raining yet again.
'Katanya' = 'they say / I heard' – marks retold info: 'katanya dia pindah' = I heard he moved.
'Kata' + person = 'according to': 'kata Ibu' = Mom says. 'Katanya' alone = generic hearsay.
'Ceritanya' = 'the story goes' – opens an anecdote: 'ceritanya dia mau memberi kejutan' = the story goes he wanted to give a surprise.
'Pokoknya' = 'anyway, bottom line' – skips the details: 'pokoknya kami selamat' = anyway, we made it.
'Kabarnya' = 'word has it' – rumor from no one in particular: 'kabarnya mereka pindah' = word is they moved.
'Tiba-tiba' = suddenly, you see it happen; 'tahu-tahu' = you only notice the result: 'tahu-tahu sudah malam' = it's night before you know it.
'Tahu-tahu' = 'before you know it': 'tahu-tahu sudah pagi' = suddenly it was morning (time slipped by).
'Tinggal' here = 'only ... left': 'tinggal bungkusnya' = only the wrapper is left; 'tinggal satu' = one left.
'Ujung-ujungnya' = 'in the end (predictably)': 'ujung-ujungnya saya yang membayar' = in the end, of course, I paid.
Doubling a verb often makes it aimless/casual: 'melihat-lihat' = just browsing, 'jalan-jalan' = stroll around.
'Dua-duanya' = both of them: 'dua-duanya salah' = both are wrong; 'tiga-tiganya' = all three.
'Sempat' = managed to fit it in: 'sempat memotret' = got the chance to snap it before it was too late.
'Sempat' before a feeling marks it as momentary: 'sempat bingung' = got confused for a bit. The feeling came and then passed.
'Sempat' also = 'at some point did': 'sempat bekerja di Bali' = worked in Bali for a time.
'Malah' marks doing the opposite of what's expected: 'disuruh tidur, dia malah menonton' = told to sleep, he watches instead.
'Lho' is a spoken surprise word, heard everywhere: 'lho, kamu di sini?' = huh, you're here? Understand it – no need to use it.
'Kok' (spoken) = 'how come?': 'kok belum tidur?' = how come you're not asleep? 'Kenapa' is the neutral word.
'Gara-gara' = 'all because of' (blaming tone): 'gara-gara macet' = all because of the traffic jam.
'Salah' + verb = did it wrong: 'salah naik' = took the wrong one, 'salah kirim' = sent it to the wrong person.
'Ter-' often means 'by accident': 'tertukar' = got swapped, 'tertinggal' = got left behind.
'Pas' (spoken) = 'right when / just as': 'pas saya mau membayar' = just as I was about to pay.
'Rupanya' = 'apparently, so it turns out' – the moment truth clicks: 'rupanya dia sudah tahu' = turns out he knew.
